---
title: "Units of assignment"
---

Suppose an experiment compares novel-talker keyword recognition after multi-talker exposure to Chinese-accented English with recognition after a control exposure. Each listener completes 40 test trials, so a study with 24 listeners produces 960 rows. What receives the exposure condition?

The answer is the listener, not the trial. Exposure happens once, before any of the 40 test responses are collected. The [**unit of assignment**](https://openstax.org/books/introductory-statistics-2e/pages/1-4-experimental-design-and-ethics), also called the *experimental unit*, is the smallest entity that can independently receive a condition under the actual procedure. Identifying this unit is the first step in reconstructing what was randomized and how many independent assignments the study contains.

## Assignment and observation are different maps

Let $r$ index rows in the recorded table. Each row belongs to an assignment unit $g(r)$, and that unit receives condition $Z_{g(r)}$. The condition attached to row $r$ is thus

$$
Z_r=Z_{g(r)}.
$$

When the listener is the unit of assignment, every row from the same listener has the same value of $g(r)$ and the same assigned condition. If there are $N=960$ rows but $G=24$ listeners, then there are 24 independent assignments, not 960. The rows remain useful because they measure each listener repeatedly. But they do not multiply the number of times exposure was assigned.

The [**unit of observation**](https://bookdown.org/pkaldunn/Book/UnitsObsAnalysis.html) answers a different question. It is the entity represented by one measured response, here a listener's keyword response on one test sentence. The [unit of analysis](../foundations/linguistic-data.qmd) describes the entities compared by a particular statistical calculation. And the **sampling unit** is the entity drawn when we sample from a target population, such as a listener recruited from a community or a sentence selected from a pool of materials. These units can coincide, but they need not. The earlier [prediction-target page](../model-criticism-and-prediction/prediction-targets.qmd) makes a related but separate choice: its *prediction unit* is the kind of new row or group to which a fitted model must transfer.

## Working through a small study

Consider four listeners, each of whom responds to three test sentences.

| listener | exposure | sentence | keyword correct |
|:--|:--|:--|--:|
| P1 | multi-talker | s1 | 1 |
| P1 | multi-talker | s2 | 1 |
| P1 | multi-talker | s3 | 0 |
| P2 | control | s1 | 0 |
| P2 | control | s2 | 1 |
| P2 | control | s3 | 0 |
| P3 | multi-talker | s1 | 1 |
| P3 | multi-talker | s2 | 1 |
| P3 | multi-talker | s3 | 1 |
| P4 | control | s1 | 1 |
| P4 | control | s2 | 0 |
| P4 | control | s3 | 0 |

There are 12 observations because 12 keyword responses were recorded. There are only four assignment units because exposure condition could vary independently only across listeners. The assignment counts are two multi-talker and two control listeners. There are also three sampled sentence items. Repeating each sentence across listeners gives information about that sentence; it does not turn the three sentences into 12 independently sampled items.

We can recover both counts from the table.

```{r}
trials <- data.frame(
  listener = rep(paste0("P", 1:4), each = 3),
  exposure = rep(c("multi_talker", "control", "multi_talker", "control"), each = 3),
  sentence = rep(paste0("s", 1:3), times = 4),
  correct = c(1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0)
)

nrow(trials)
listener_assignment <- unique(trials[c("listener", "exposure")])
nrow(listener_assignment)
table(listener_assignment$exposure)
```

The call to `unique()` implements the definition above. It retains one row for each distinct assignment unit and its condition. A design audit should perform this reduction before counting assignments.

## Asking what could have varied independently

The most reliable diagnostic is counterfactual and procedural: under the actual assignment procedure, what could have received a different condition? In the exposure study, one test trial could not switch exposure while the other trials from the same listener remained unchanged. The listener is thus the assignment unit.

The same question applies at other levels. If an instructional intervention is assigned by classroom and responses are collected from individual students, the classroom is the assignment unit. If an acoustic manipulation is applied once to an entire recording, the recording is the assignment unit even when several acoustic measurements are extracted from it. And if an item version is independently chosen for each presentation, the presentation may be the assignment unit, subject to the participant and list constraints imposed by the design.

## Response rows do not count assignments

Treating the unit represented by a row as an independent assignment unit would count 960 assignments rather than 24. The resulting uncertainty would appear too small because responses sharing one assignment are treated as if exposure had been assigned repeatedly. This is the same dependence problem developed for [repeated linguistic observations](../regression-models/structured-data.qmd), now stated in terms of the assignment procedure.

The number of response rows does not change the number of independent condition assignments. A model may represent the fact that responses share participants, but it cannot create assignment variation that the experiment did not produce.

## Writing the design in three sentences

Before collection, write one sentence for each unit.

1. One row of the raw data represents one keyword response to one test sentence.
2. Exposure condition is assigned once to each listener.
3. Responses are repeated within listeners and sentences; test talkers may create a third grouping if several talkers are sampled.

This compact description exposes the design before model notation obscures it. It also records which repeated units the earlier [mixed effects models](../regression-models/structured-data.qmd) must preserve when they are applied to this study.

::: {.callout-note title="Audit the assignment unit"}
1. A classroom receives a teaching method, and each student supplies five responses. What is the assignment unit, and what is the observation unit?
2. A participant hears 60 words, with accent independently selected for each word subject to equal condition counts. What could receive a different condition under the procedure?
3. Why can additional trials improve measurement without adding independent assignments?
:::

The unit of assignment is the smallest entity whose condition could vary independently under the actual design. Separating it from observation, analysis, and sampling units fixes both the level at which assignment operates and the populations over which a later claim might generalize.
